$schema-note: Every difference between a v9 frame and the implementation lands in exactly one class. Gate B reads this file and enforces the rules below — the classification is not advisory prose.

classes.MUST-FIX: Clearly violates v9 with no functionality or accessibility reason. Implement the v9 design exactly. BLOCKS its frame until closed. No approval needed to fix — fixing toward v9 is the mandate.
classes.APPROVED-DEVIATION: Existing functionality or accessibility requires something different from v9. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.PRODUCT-DECISION: The v9 HTML specifies a different workflow or different copy, and choosing between them is the owner's call, not an engineering one. DO NOT MODIFY until the owner explicitly approves. Blocks its frame while status is pending.
classes.NOT-BUILT: The surface or its server support does not exist yet. Leave untouched until its assigned migration task runs. Does not block a frame for a defect it cannot have.

deviations.summary: Geist Sans/Mono retained instead of the spec's system font stack
deviations.reason: The system stack renders as SF Pro on iOS and Roboto on Android — two different products. Sizes, weights and tracking follow the spec exactly.
deviations.measuredCost: Geist runs ~5% wider per glyph at 800. Measured on frame 07 at the spec's own values (27px/800/-0.02em, 22px gutters, 326px available): Geist 336px vs the system stack 320px. So the .ob-q question WRAPS TO TWO LINES where frames 07 and 08 set it on one.
deviations.openQuestion: See deviation 19 — the wrap is tracked separately so it can be ruled on without reopening the font choice.

deviations.summary: design-system.md §12.1 reversed: ambient wash allowed app-wide, mascot allowed on working screens
deviations.reason: The v9 spec reverses two Phase-2.6 rules. Its own mascot law bans Odo only from money and safety surfaces.

deviations.summary: 5 tabs → 4 tabs + /more hub
deviations.reason: The v9 nav is 4 tabs plus the orb in every frame. No route removed.

deviations.summary: WebAuthn descoped pre-launch; frame 06 out of scope
deviations.reason: Browser inconsistency and support burden outweigh the MVP security delta.

deviations.summary: Patient tab renamed "Tooth Map" → "Teeth"
deviations.reason: Matches the spec's .ptabs row.
deviations.note: APPROVED BUT NOT YET IMPLEMENTED — app/(app)/patients/[id]/page.tsx still reads 'Tooth Map'. Task 22 owns the change.

deviations.summary: Clinic creation kept as 3 steps; the frame shows a single screen
deviations.reason: The single screen drops hours and profile capture. Feature parity outranks fidelity.
deviations.openQuestion: AMBIGUOUS AS WRITTEN. The frame's model is one QUESTION at a time ("What's your clinic called?" → "Next · City"), while our step 1 holds six fields. "Keep 3 steps" does not settle whether step 1 should be one question or six fields — those are different claims.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the 3-step workflow, but redesign each step to the v9 one-question-at-a-time pattern with a destination-labelled CTA. Do NOT collapse the required data collection. Step 1 must not remain a dense six-field form.
deviations.fixedIn: Step 1 now asks ONE QUESTION AT A TIME — five screens on one route: name -> contact -> address -> city+state -> pincode+GST, each with the `.field` hero input and a CTA naming its destination. All three steps and all seven fields survive; only the pacing changed. The question list lives in lib/ds/wizard with a test asserting every key of stepBasicsSchema appears exactly once, so re-pacing can never silently drop a field. Back walks the questions before leaving the step, so one tap no longer discards four answers. 8.7% -> 5.1%.

deviations.summary: No summoned numeric keypad on /phone
deviations.reason: The page has always used the native keyboard; building a pad adds a surface rather than migrating one.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the keypad. Implement v9 visually and behaviourally, preserving phone validation and rate-limit logic.
deviations.fixedIn: Built as `NumericKeypad` from the spec's `.keypad`/`.key` CSS: 48px keys, radius 12, white, 0 3px 10px shadow, 19px/600 digits over 8.5px/700 letter rows, ghost bottom corners. Real <button>s, so it is keyboard-reachable and screen-reader announced, and the native keyboard still works underneath. It only produces digits — IndianPhone.safeParse still gates the CTA and rate-limit handling is untouched.

deviations.summary: /more shows 3 module tiles for a doctor, not 4
deviations.reason: canAccess('/billing','DOCTOR') is false. Rendering it would leak a permission — an access-control requirement, not a style choice.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — 3 tiles. RBAC determines available actions; no inaccessible fourth tile for symmetry.

deviations.summary: /lab/new kept as a page; the frame shows a sheet
deviations.reason: Feature parity.
deviations.ruling: USE the sheet presentation for lab creation. Preserve every existing field, validation rule, API call and workflow. Presentation only.

deviations.summary: Patient detail keeps 5 tabs (Media has no frame)
deviations.reason: Feature parity — Media must not disappear.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep 5 tabs including Media.

deviations.summary: Mascot rendered on /role; frame 07 has none
deviations.reason: Introduced without cause during migration and never flagged.

deviations.summary: /role used tap→navigate; frame 07 is select→sticky CTA "Continue as doctor"
deviations.reason: A different interaction model, shipped unflagged.

deviations.summary: Phone number masked to "+91 ••••• 0001"; frame 04 shows it in full
deviations.reason: Shoulder-surfing protection on a screen a patient may see. A workflow/privacy choice, not styling.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep masking. Recorded as a deviation FROM v9, not a match to it: frame 04 shows the number in full ("Sent to +91 98401 23456 · Edit") and v9 specifies no masking anywhere. The intent in both the table ("KEEP masking") and the prose ("do not expose the complete phone number") is unambiguous, so the mask stays and the departure is on the record.

deviations.summary: An explicit "Verify" button; frames 04/05 auto-submit on the sixth digit
deviations.reason: Accessibility: SMS autofill does not always fire, and a screen-reader or keyboard user needs an explicit submit target. Auto-submit alone leaves no way to retry a corrected code.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the Verify button. Functional UI is not removed to reduce a pixel percentage.

deviations.summary: A wrong code clears the six boxes; frame 05 keeps the digits inside crit outlines
deviations.reason: No functionality or accessibility reason to clear. The frame keeps the digits precisely so the user can see and fix the typo; clearing forces a full re-entry.

deviations.summary: /welcome carousel has 4 slides with different copy, a Skip link and language chips; frame 02 is slide 1 of 3 with none of those
deviations.reason: The frame's slide-1 copy ('Speak. Odovox writes the record.') is the product's opening promise. Which pitch opens the app is a product call.
deviations.ruling: MATCH v9. Frame 02 has THREE dots, NO Skip link and NO language chips, and its note reads "3 swipeable value dots; CTA skips them" — so the Skip behaviour IS the CTA, which goes straight to /phone. Implement: v9 slide-1 copy, 3 slides, no separate Skip link, no chips, CTA always "Continue with phone".
deviations.fixedIn: 3 slides with frame 02's slide-1 copy verbatim, no Skip link (the CTA carries that job, per the frame's own note "CTA skips them"), no language chips, 3 dots. Layout re-anchored to the frame's top-down flow — 56px above Odo, 18px to the question, dots 20px under the body, CTA at the floor — replacing a vertically centred group that sat ~70px low. 10.0% -> 2.8%.

deviations.summary: /clinic-join is a two-field form + explicit "Find clinic"; frame 09 is one hero code field with a live check and a clinic preview
deviations.reason: Two things at once: the joiner's name is feature parity (the request records who is asking), and the lookup model differs (explicit press vs validate-as-you-type).
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the two-field lookup. Recreate the v9 visual treatment around the existing reliable workflow.

deviations.summary: The Odo mascot artwork was not the spec's #odo-body symbol
deviations.reason: The spec draws an outline tooth with lime blush ovals; the app drew a filled grey tooth with no blush. Systemic.

deviations.summary: The .ob-q question wraps to two lines where frames 07 and 08 set it on one
deviations.reason: A measured consequence of approved deviation 1, not an independent defect — the app matches the spec's values exactly. Closing it means altering one of the spec's own numbers.
deviations.openQuestion: (a) accept the wrap, (b) drop the question to ~25.5px, or (c) tighten question tracking to about -0.0355em.
deviations.ruling: MATCH the v9 wrap. Verify in order: font family, weight, container width, size, line height; use letter-spacing only if needed.
deviations.fixedIn: Applied in the ruling's own order. Items 2-5 already matched the spec exactly (800 weight, 326px container, 27px, 1.15 leading), and item 1 is approved deviation 1, so letter-spacing was the only remaining lever: new --tracking-question token at -0.036em, scoped to the .ob-q heading alone. The rest of the app keeps the spec's -0.02em. Verified in the browser: "How will you use Odovox?" now renders on ONE line at 326px.

deviations.summary: A lime focus ring on the .field; the frame's focused field has none
deviations.reason: Accessibility. Removing focus indication to win pixels is a real regression for keyboard users.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the focus ring. Make it restrained and consistent with the v9 system.

deviations.summary: A "By continuing you agree to our terms." line; frame 03 has none
deviations.reason: Legal copy, not styling. Whether it may be removed is not an engineering call.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the terms/legal copy. Style it with v9 typography and spacing.
deviations.fixedIn: Restyled to the v9 system: 12px/600 on --pine-3, directly under the keypad.

deviations.summary: No .mic-a affordance on /phone
deviations.reason: useDictation presigns an upload and calls an AUTHENTICATED transcription endpoint; /phone is pre-login by definition. Needs an unauthenticated dictation route that does not exist. A mic that does nothing is worse than no mic.

deviations.summary: A "Wrong code. N attempts left." toast on top of the frame's inline message
deviations.reason: The frame reports the failure once, inline. The toast reports it twice — but it also carries the remaining-attempts count, which is information the frame does not show and which warns of lockout. Dropping it loses that warning.
deviations.ruling: KEEP the attempts-left toast. Restyle to the v9 visual language.

deviations.summary: WITHDRAWN — false finding. Resend already unlocks immediately on a wrong code.
deviations.reason: The verify catch already calls setSecondsLeft(0), so "Resend code" renders at once, exactly as frame 05 specifies. The first review read "Resend in 1:00" off a capture taken BEFORE the error state was reached — the A5 prepare step was silently failing, so the screenshot was of the clean OTP screen. Fixing the prepare step invalidated the finding.

deviations.summary: A dotted texture sits behind the resend area; frames 04/05 have none
deviations.reason: Pure decoration with no functional or accessibility role.

deviations.summary: Step 1 is missing frame 08's .ob-dots, verified-identity chip and defaults card, and its CTA reads "Continue →" not "Next · City"
deviations.reason: All four are v9 elements the app simply does not render. Independent of deviation 6 — keeping three steps says nothing about dropping the frame's furniture from step 1.

deviations.summary: The back control carries a "Join a clinic" text label and a stray Odo sits top-right
deviations.reason: Frame 09 uses a bare white IconCircle and has no mascot. Both are additions, not workflow.

deviations.summary: Availability's "2 doctors" and Team's "1 request" values are absent
deviations.reason: Both need a clinic-members endpoint. /clinics has only create, lookup and join — there is no members or pending-requests route to read. Task 31 owns that server work.

deviations.summary: A voice search field on /home; frame 13 has none
deviations.reason: Existing functionality. /patients carries its own search (frame 33), so this may be duplication — but it is not deleted without a ruling. Kept and restyled into the v9 language under a labelled section.
deviations.ruling: DROP — no voice search on Home; Patients owns patient search.

deviations.summary: The VoiceCommandHero on /home; frame 13 has none
deviations.reason: Existing functionality. In v9 the dock's orb is the voice surface, so this is likely duplication — but removing a working voice entry point is a product call.
deviations.ruling: DROP — no VoiceCommandHero; the dock orb remains the single global voice affordance.

deviations.summary: Five quick tiles where frame 13 has three (Lab, Schedule, Block time)
deviations.reason: New patient and Inventory are the two extra. Both are reachable from /more and the speed dial, so the frame may be right that they do not belong on Flow — but dropping them changes the doctor's daily reach.
deviations.ruling: DROP — do not duplicate the two quick actions already available through More/speed dial.

deviations.summary: A 'Recent' section on /home; frame 13 has none
deviations.reason: Existing functionality, and the only place recent visits surface outside a patient record.
deviations.ruling: KEEP — Recent section remains on Home.

deviations.summary: The hero ring shows a placeholder dot, not the sitting count (frame 13: 2/3)
deviations.reason: The queue visit carries no treatment-plan context, so sitting n/N is not available on /home. Needs the active plan joined onto the in-chair visit — server work Task 22 (patient plans) or a /home aggregate would own.

deviations.summary: The hero subtitle reads queue context, not the frame's clinical line
deviations.reason: Frame 13 reads 'RCT 36 · obturation today · penicillin allergy' — procedure, today's step, and the allergy in crit. Ours reads 'Now treating X · N waiting'. The clinical line needs the plan and allergy joined onto the in-chair visit; same missing join as #33.

deviations.summary: A back chevron in the /consult header; frame 21 has none
deviations.reason: /consult is not one of the four dock tabs — it is reached from Flow's 'Continue consultation'. Removing back would strand anyone who arrived that way. Navigation, not decoration.
deviations.ruling: KEEP — back chevron remains on Consult because Consult is not a dock destination.

deviations.summary: A ProfileButton in the /consult header; frame 21 has none
deviations.reason: Account is reachable from /more, so this may be duplication — but it is existing functionality and not deleted without a ruling.
deviations.ruling: APPROVED — keep the profile icon on /consult.

deviations.summary: The in-chair card shows an elapsed timer; frame 21 does not
deviations.reason: How long the patient has been in the chair is real clinical information and was already on this screen. The frame omits it, so keeping it is a departure — but dropping it loses a signal a doctor uses.
deviations.ruling: KEEP — elapsed consultation timer remains.

deviations.summary: No "₹ Due" filter chip; frame 32 has one
deviations.reason: There is no outstanding-balance filter on the API — PatientFilter is all/in_chair/due_today/lab_pending/recent. A chip that silently returned the unfiltered list would be worse than its absence, so it is not rendered. Needs a server filter.
deviations.ruling: Becomes a real feature, not a visual fake. Task 34 adds a `balanceDue` filter to the patients list — server, types and chip — because reception needs to list who owes money, not because a frame draws a chip. Built with the billing work, not for the screenshot.

deviations.summary: Two filter chips the frame does not show — Lab and Recent
deviations.reason: Both are existing filters with server support. The frame shows four chips; we show five (six once ₹ Due exists). Trimming is a product call, not a styling one.
deviations.ruling: KEEP — Lab and Recent filters remain because they correspond to real server-supported filters.

deviations.summary: An "All patients · N" section header above the list; frame 32 goes straight to the card
deviations.reason: The count is useful and was on the old screen. The frame omits it.
deviations.ruling: DROP — remove the redundant "All patients · N" header.

generalRule: Functionality, security, RBAC, accessibility and legal requirements are never removed for pixel-level fidelity. Where a deviation is approved, preserve the functionality and reproduce the v9 visual language around it. No additional deviation is created without asking first.
rule: EVERY COMPLETED TASK LEAVES ZERO OPEN PRODUCT-DECISION ITEMS FOR THAT TASK. Open decisions are raised and resolved within the task that surfaced them. They are never carried forward: a pile of 20-30 unresolved deviations at the end is a pile nobody can remember the reason for.
